offences.quote: Unauthorised or unacknowledged use of Generative Artificial Intelligence(GenAI) or other computer assistance – this includes any unauthorised or unacknowledged use of GenAI, paraphrasing/translation software, or other computer assistance such that the work submitted, including referencing, cannot be considered wholly the student’s own.

Unauthorised or unacknowledged use of Generative Artificial Intelligence(GenAI) or other computer assistance – this includes any unauthorised or unacknowledged use of GenAI, paraphrasing/translation software, or other computer assistance such that the work submitted, including referencing, cannot be considered wholly the student’s own.
Plagiarism – presenting for assessment someone else’s work or ideas as the student’s own.

Self-plagiarism – submitting for assessment the same work that the student has previously submitted at Loughborough, or which has contributed to an award at any other institution, unless specific provision for this is made in the assessment brief.
Contract cheating – engaging a third party to complete assessed work for a student who then submits it as their own.
Collusion – working with another student on an assessment which is intended to be the student’s own work.
Assisting another student to gain an advantage by unfair means or receiving such assistance, for example by impersonation
Obtaining and/or distributing a copy of another student’s work without their permission.
Falsifying or fabricating data, evidence, or experimental results in assessed work.
Failing to comply with the rules for Written Examination Candidates (in Regulation VII), including possession of prohibited materials or technology during an examination, class-test, or equivalent.

process.quote: Any circumstances which appear to suggest that a candidate has committed a minor act of academic misconduct will be reported to the Chair and Secretary of the Minor Academic Misconduct Committee for the School responsible for the module in question
The candidate will be invited to admit or deny the allegation, and permitted to defend themselves in writing and/or in person, accompanied by an individual of their own choosing.
Candidates may submit a written defence and any other written evidence, attend the Committee meeting in person accompanied by an individual of their own choosing and call witnesses.
The candidate will be invited to admit or deny the allegation, and permitted to defend themselves in writing and/or in person, accompanied by an individual of their own choosing.

Students found guilty of either minor or major offences shall have the right of appeal against the decision taken and/or penalties imposed by the Minor Academic Misconduct Committee or the University’s Academic Misconduct Committee.
Appeals must normally be submitted within 10 working days of the date on which the student was informed of the outcome of the academic misconduct meeting.

outcomes.quote: The issue of a formal reprimand.
The reduction by any amount of any or all of the marks obtained by the candidate in any module in the current part of the candidate's programme.
To set a cap on any mark achieved by the candidate on reassessment in any module in the current part of the candidate's programme.
The immediate termination of the candidate's studies.

In exceptional circumstances, where a student is found guilty of a first offence of academic misconduct in relation to a module undertaken on a second attempt basis, the Committee may permit the student to resubmit the work in which academic misconduct was found, at the next available opportunity

A candidate suspected of committing a minor offence will automatically be referred for action under the major offence procedure if s/he has previously been found guilty of any offence of academic misconduct, or is suspected of an offence in more than one assessed element of his/her programme.
Suspected incidents of academic misconduct will be defined as minor or major depending on their seriousness.

Having taken into account the evidence and the defence, if any, the Minor Academic Misconduct Committee will decide whether the candidate is guilty of the offence, and if so, what penalty should be imposed.

definitions.quote: The University defines academic misconduct as any action by a student which gives or has the potential to give them or any other student an unfair advantage in any examination or assessment
Plagiarism – presenting for assessment someone else’s work or ideas as the student’s own.

Contract cheating – engaging a third party to complete assessed work for a student who then submits it as their own.
Collusion – working with another student on an assessment which is intended to be the student’s own work.
